title: Edge Workers LLM proxy — polyglot sample pack for streaming & retry ergonomics
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Deliver a cohesive, opinionated sample pack that demonstrates production-ready patterns for using Redwood SDKs at the edge and server-side: Next.js (Edge and Node runtimes), FastAPI, a lightweight Go HTTP server, and a CLI for local developer workflows.

Focus areas: streaming ergonomics (SSE vs chunked transfer vs WebSocket), incremental decoding and token buffering, robust retry/backoff for transient network and 5xx model responses, and graceful degradation strategies when the preferred model or variant is unavailable.

Samples will include: a Next.js Edge function that proxies streaming responses with minimal cold-start overhead; a Next.js Node API route that shows chunked streaming and server-side buffering; a FastAPI sample using async generator streaming and background tasks to manage KV cache warming; a Go HTTP server demonstrating net/http flusher-based streaming and context cancel handling; and a small CLI that consumes streaming output with resumable retries and progress indicators.

The pack should be opinionated: provide recommended defaults for retry counts/timeouts, backoff strategy, max in-flight tokens, and examples of integrating Redwood Optimize recommendations (e.g., quantization suggestion hints) via comments and metadata in the examples.

decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Use chunked transfer (HTTP/1.1) for server-to-browser streaming in Node runtime and SSE for edge-optimized flows where the client expects event framing. Rationale: chunked transfer gives slightly lower overhead on Node, SSE fits well with Next.js Edge runtime's streaming limitations and has broader client support without WebSocket handshakes.

Tradeoff: WebSocket provides bidirectional low-latency streams but increases complexity for simple one-way generation flows; deferred in favor of chunked/SSE for these samples to keep developer mental model simple.

Decision: Implement resumable streaming using deterministic sequence hashes + server-side short-lived resume tokens. Rationale: simpler than full stateful checkpointing and interoperable across runtimes. Requires instrumenting example servers to emit resume metadata headers when applicable.
review_feedback: PM (Janelle Ortiz): tighten the onboarding path — lead with the smallest reproducible example (CLI) before showing full-stack Next.js flows.
Design (Marco Silva): clarify UX for partial output in browser — show a small spinner/activity indicator while upstream generates first N tokens and avoid content jumps.

Security (Noah Patel): recommend default TLS + validate upstream model certs and call out KMS usage for Private deployments in README. Also requested a short checklist for required permissions when deploying FastAPI/Go examples to customer VPCs.
Engineering (Rosa Kim): add a test that simulates delayed token emission to validate buffering thresholds; suggested a 50ms inter-token jitter test.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Edge runtime cold starts could add latency and impact perceived streaming smoothness. Mitigation: recommend minimal warmers for production and present fallbacks to Node runtime when tail latency matters.
Risk: Resume tokens leak state. Mitigation: short TTL tokens and sign tokens with server secret; examples include notes to rotate keys and not store tokens long-term.

Risk: Different runtimes handle chunk boundaries differently leading to client parsing inconsistencies. Mitigation: include strict tests for chunk framing and provide helper parsers in each sample (TS/Python/Go).
